question.:question/problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}3 \ln{\left(u v w \right)} \\ - 4 u + w \\ 4 u v\end{aligned}].
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have 

$$
x(u,v,w)=3 \ln{\left(u v w \right)}\, y(u,v,w)=- 4 u + w\, z(u,v,w)=4 u v.
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =\frac{3}{u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & =\frac{3}{v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} & =\frac{3}{w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =-4 & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & =0 & \frac{∂y}{∂w} & =1 \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & =4 v & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & =4 u, & \frac{∂z}{∂w} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{u} & \frac{3}{v} & \frac{3}{w} \\ -4 & 0 & 1 \\ 4 v & 4 u & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =\left(\frac{3}{w}\right)(-1)^{1+3}|\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 \\ 4 v & 4 u\end{aligned}|+\left(1\right)(-1)^{2+3}|\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{u} & \frac{3}{v} \\ 4 v & 4 u\end{aligned}| \\  & =\left(\frac{3}{w}\right)\left(- 16 u-\left(0\right)\right)+\left(-1\right)\left(12-\left(12\right)\right) \\  & =- \frac{48 u}{w}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
x(u,v,w)=- 3 u e^{w}\, y(u,v,w)=- u - 3 w\, z(u,v,w)=- 4 v + w e^{u}.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =- 3 e^{w} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & =0 & \frac{∂x}{∂w} & =- 3 u e^{w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =-1 & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & =0 & \frac{∂y}{∂w} & =-3 \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & =w e^{u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & =-4, & \frac{∂z}{∂w} & =e^{u}\end{aligned}
